transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I suppose what brings me in is that I’m frightened by how I get around food. I don’t mean just enjoying a meal or having a little too much, I mean once I start eating, it’s like something in me doesn’t listen anymore. My hands just keep reaching for more, one thing after another, even while I’m sitting there thinking — telling myself, really — “Tom, stop this right now.” And I do mean I’m telling myself that, in my own head, very clearly.

But it doesn’t seem to matter in the moment. That’s the part that scares me most, I think. It feels like I’m not fully in charge once it starts, like I can see myself doing it and I know I should stop, but I don’t. I’m 78 years old and I feel embarrassed even saying that out loud, but that loss of control is what’s been weighing on me.
Do these episodes of eating like this happen even when you’re not hungry, or do they usually happen in situations that make you feel especially upset or stressed?

I’m not sure I can give you a clean answer to that, doctor. I’ve tried to think about it, but it doesn’t always seem to line up neatly in my mind.

Sometimes I don’t think I’m properly hungry, not in the ordinary sense of “I missed lunch and my stomach is empty.” It can be more like… the food is there, or I’ve started with something small, and then it gathers speed before I’ve really taken stock of whether I was hungry in the first place. But other times I tell myself I must have been hungry, because I hadn’t eaten much earlier, or because it was around a normal mealtime. So I get muddled about it.

As for being upset or stressed, I don’t know. I wouldn’t say every time there’s some big emotional event beforehand. I’m an old man, so there are plenty of thoughts rattling around in the background, and I can be tense without even naming it. But I haven’t noticed a simple pattern like, “Oh, I had a bad phone call, so then it happened.” It’s more slippery than that. I suppose I mostly notice the episode once it’s already underway, and by then I’m not carefully tracing what started it.
After these episodes of eating, do you find yourself feeling physically uncomfortable, guilty, or distressed about what happened?

I’m not completely sure how to answer that in a tidy way. I mean… yes, I suppose sometimes I feel uncomfortable after, but I don’t always know whether I’d call it physical discomfort in the way you might mean. I can feel sort of heavy or unsettled, and then I start thinking about what just happened, and that can sit with me.

The guilt part is harder to admit, because it sounds childish at my age, doesn’t it? But I do get this feeling afterward of, “Why did I do that again?” There’s a kind of disappointment in myself. I’ll look back over it and think I should have been able to stop sooner, or I shouldn’t have let it go that far. But I’m not sure I can separate guilt from embarrassment or distress. It all blends together a bit.

I wouldn’t say every single time is exactly the same. Sometimes I’m more numb afterward, like I don’t want to think about it too closely. Other times I feel quite bothered by it, and I’ll sort of replay it in my head. So… yes, there’s often something unpleasant afterward, but I’m not sure I can put a precise name to it.

After these episodes of eating, do you ever try to compensate in any way — like making yourself sick, using laxatives, or exercising a lot more than usual — because you're worried about gaining weight?

Yes… yes, I have. I don’t like saying it, but there have been times after I’ve eaten too much where I go to the bathroom and make myself bring it back up.

It’s not something I’m proud of. Usually by then I’m frightened the food is going to stay in me, if that makes sense, and I start thinking about gaining weight and feeling like I have to undo what I just did. So I’ll make myself sick.

And I’ve taken laxatives too, for the same reason. Not because a doctor told me to or anything like that — it’s more this panicked feeling afterward that I need to get the food out of me somehow. I know it sounds awful, especially at my age, but that’s what happens sometimes.
How often do these episodes happen, and would you say they occur regularly or more like every now and then?

It’s been… regular, I think. More regular than I’d like to admit.

I started keeping food logs some time ago, partly because I thought if I wrote it down I’d understand it better, or maybe catch myself before it went too far. And looking back at those, it’s not just an occasional odd day here and there. For many months now, nearly every week there’s been at least one afternoon where I’ve eaten in that out-of-control way, and then afterward I’ve tried to make up for it somehow.

Sometimes that’s by making myself sick. Sometimes I’ve used laxatives. Other times I’ll decide I’m not going to eat for a while afterward, or I’ll push myself to walk more than I probably should, or keep doing chores longer than I need to, like I’m trying to work it off. It tends to be afternoons, for whatever reason. I don’t know if that’s just when I’m alone with it more, or when the day catches up with me, but that’s what the logs show.

So no, I wouldn’t say it’s just every now and then. It’s been happening nearly weekly, at least, for months.
Do you find yourself especially worried about your body shape or weight, and does that concern come up often when you think about these episodes of eating?

Yes… that’s a big part of it, I think. Maybe the biggest part, if I’m being honest.

I know this may not make much sense from the outside, because my doctor has told me I’m too thin. More than once. And I can hear that, intellectually, I suppose. I understand the words. But it doesn’t feel true to me when I’m looking at the scale or thinking about what I ate. If the number is even up by half a pound, I get this awful panicky feeling, like something has gone wrong and I’ve let myself go. Half a pound — I know how small that sounds — but it can feel enormous to me in the moment.

And then I feel ashamed, not just worried. It’s like I’ve failed at keeping control of myself. After one of those eating episodes, that’s often what my mind goes straight to: “What has this done to my weight?” or “How much damage have I caused?” I’ll think I need to fix it right away, before it gets worse. It becomes very urgent in my head, even if part of me knows I’m probably not thinking reasonably.

So yes, my weight and shape are there in the background a lot. It’s not just afterward, but afterward is when it gets especially loud.
